title: picard_residue_homology_source_fibre_comparison
statement:
Under the complete signature below, the derived residue fibre of the direct image of the pulled-back line bundle is additively equivalent to degree-one structure-sheaf cohomology of X_s; no affine representative is assumed.

Exact Lean statement:
theorem picard_residue_homology_source_fibre_comparison
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{v},
      HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1} (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {X S : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (W : Scheme.{v}) (k : W ⟶ S) [IsImmersion k]
    (w : W) (s : S) (hw : k w = s)
    (τ : (Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecResidueField s))).obj L ≅
      SheafOfModules.unit (pullback f (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).ringCatSheaf)
    :
    let E := (schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd f k)).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings (pullback f k).toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
          ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f k)).obj L))
    Nonempty (derivedFiberCohomology W E 1 w ≃+
      Sheaf.H (structureSheafAb (pullback f (S.fromSpecResidueField s))) 1)

source.place: Tags 0A1D, 0B91, 0BF2 and 01XK; derived base change, fibre trivialization and affine-base sections

proof.text: Use exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction and uniqueness of left adjoints to identify tensor pullback with ordinary module pullback. Ordinary pullback preserves invertibility; transport this instance across the comparison and use IsInvertible.sheafOfModules_isInvertible to obtain the sheaf-module invertibility required by the canonical comparisons.

For a flat quasi-compact separated q:Y→W and invertible M, apply isIso_derivedBaseChange_of_flat_invertible to its pullback along W.fromSpecResidueField w. Compose its isomorphism with the derived direct image of isIso_canonicalSinglePullbackMap. This identifies the derived residue pullback of Rq_*(M[0]) with Rp_*((a^*M)[0]), where a and p are the fibre projections. This is the first half of the proved private helper derivedFiberDirectImageCohomology.

Apply DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor in degree n and Functor.homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso for RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage p. The latter is the proved source-library computation of the defining unbounded direct-image functor on a module placed in degree zero (PlusCompatibility.lean). Evaluate sections on the residue spectrum; restriction of scalars in derivedFiberCohomology does not change its additive group. Enough injectives on the fibre gives injective resolutions. The ordinary pulled module is invertible, hence quasi-coherent. Apply nonempty_sections_higherDirectImage_iso_H over the affine residue spectrum. This completes derivedFiberDirectImageCohomology.

Substitute hw. Surjectivity of the immersion stalk map and of the residue quotient proves surjectivity of k.residueFieldMap w in three lines; its field-ring-hom injectivity proves it is an isomorphism. Mathlib SpecMap_residueFieldMap_fromSpecResidueField gives residue-point naturality. pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso and pullback.map along the spectrum isomorphism give the fibre isomorphism e, with its projection equation by simp. Convert tensor pullbacks to ordinary pullbacks using adjunction uniqueness. Compose ordinary pullbackComp and pullbackCongr along that equation, apply pullback to tau, and finish with pullbackObjUnitIso. This is the fully proved private helper exists_immersion_residue_fibre_trivialization.

Functoriality of structureSheafCohomologyPullback applied to e.hom and e.inv makes the two cohomology maps inverse; the private generic addEquivOfInverse constructs their additive equivalence without expanding the concrete maps. Modules.H.mapLinearEquiv transports cohomology along the coefficient trivialization. The unit module underlying additive sheaf is definitionally structureSheafAb. Apply derivedFiberDirectImageCohomology to pullback.snd f k (properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness after base change), and compose these three additive equivalences in degree one.
